title: Customer tail-call signal filtering and sampling-default inheritance mismatch
creator: Marco Diaz
description: High-severity customer reports of nondeterministic eval regressions after a recent serving change that altered sampling defaults and introduced a new "tail-call" filtering layer in the routing path. The regressions manifest as extra appended lines in customer JSON outputs and failing evaluation metrics for a small set of customers using Private deployments and Dedicated pools. Initial triage indicates a mismatch between per-customer sampling config inheritance and a new signal filter that strips the stop marker in some fallback paths.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer's canonical prompt (redacted) with strict JSON stop-token "<END>" in a Private pool using legacy per-tenant sampling override.
2) Send repeated requests with sampling.temperature=0.8 and sampling.top_p unspecified (should inherit legacy default).
3) Observe that in ~7% of requests the response does not include the terminal <END> marker and extra free-form text is appended, causing evals to fail.
4) Reproduce is more frequent when requests are routed through the private->hosted fallback chain during burst events.
observed_behavior: Responses occasionally omit the configured stop marker and append extra tokens; evals show downstream parsing errors and lower scoring on the customer test-set. Issue is customer-specific (appears for customers with per-tenant sampling overrides on Private pools) but can be reproduced in an internal staging Private cluster with the same config.
expected_behavior: Responses should always respect explicit stop tokens set by the customer and inherit sampling defaults consistently from the tenant config; fallback routing should not remove or remap stop signals.
root_cause_summary: The new tail-call signal filter introduced into the routing layer was intended to deduplicate trailing control tokens for hosted fallbacks. However, the filter ran before the sampling-default merge step for tenant-scoped configs in Private/Dedicated paths. When a fallback to hosted capacity occurred, the hosted path applied a different sampling default, and the filter logic interpreted the stop marker as a soft delimiter to be dropped under certain stochastic kernels. The combination produced sequences that bypassed the explicit stop token and continued generation.
mitigation: 1) Hotfix deployed to staging that reorders the config merge so tenant sampling defaults are applied before tail-call filtering. 2) Temporary rule: when a request includes an explicit stop token metadata flag, skip the tail-call filter for that request. 3) Proactively applied a rate-limited safeguard to prefer native capacity for affected tenants while we validate the fix.
testing_notes: Added deterministic regression tests that assert stop-token presence across routing fallbacks.
Added fuzz tests for sampling-default inheritance across tenant/private/hosted transitions.
Verified fixes on staging Private cluster with synthetic replay of customer traffic for 48 hours (no failures observed in 100k requests).
deployment_plan: Canary deploy fix to 10% of Private clusters tomorrow 2025-02-29, monitor token-level metrics and customer eval pass rate for 24 hours. If stable, promote to 50% then 100% across Private/Dedicated within 72 hours. Coordinate with SRE for rollback playbook.
rollback_plan: If we observe an uptick in latency or new generation regressions, rollback routing change which reintroduces pre-fix ordering and enable immediate tenant-level safelist to route affected customers to isolated capacity.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add a linting rule in CI to detect any future reorderings that could move signal filters ahead of config merges.
2) Product/PM to contact affected customers with a summary and next steps; prepare post-mortem for incident review meeting.
3) Add telemetry: emit 'stop-token-verified' boolean in tracing for every request to make regressions visible earlier.
4) Schedule a design review for routing filter contract to codify invariants across Hosted/Dedicated/Private paths.
